title: pool() can be DoS'd indefinitely if the donation phase's minUSDC requirement cannot be satisfied (USDC depeg, waUSDC redeem failure, or pool depletion), permanently locking sUSDS in the dispatcher
description:
pool() is an all-or-nothing transaction: the donation phase and the addLiquidity phase execute in a single unlockCallback. If the donation phase reverts (e.g., require(usdcReceived >= minUSDC) fails, or IERC4626(waUsdc).redeem reverts due to Aave pause / waUSDC frozen / Aave market liquidity exhaustion, or IERC20(usdc).safeTransfer(batchMinter, ...) reverts because batchMinter has been blocklisted on USDC), the entire unlockCallback reverts. There is no fallback path that skips the donation and proceeds to addLiquidity.

The dispatcher's owner has rescueERC20 as an escape hatch, which can transfer sUSDS out — but this is a centralisation lever. It is NOT an automated recovery.

Re-validation note (yield-claim-nft-07, HEAD 1bb956c): unlockCallback body byte-identical to c67d3c9; lines shifted forward by ~3 due to import addition. Finding carries forward. The new migrateMint function does NOT touch pool() / unlockCallback flow; orthogonal.
exploit_path:
Scenario A — USDC blocklist of batchMinter:
USDC's Circle administrator blacklists an address. If batchMinter happens to be that address, IERC20(usdc).safeTransfer(batchMinter, ...) reverts. Until the owner calls setBatchMinter(...) to point to a new recipient, every pool() call reverts.

Scenario B — Aave waUSDC market pause:
Aave can pause the waUSDC market. IERC4626(waUsdc).redeem(...) reverts. pool() cannot progress until Aave unpauses.

Scenario C — donation pool depletion:
If the sUSDS/waUSDC Balancer pool's waUSDC side is drained, the donation swap may revert or yield waUsdcReceived below minUSDC after unwrap.
mainnet_realism: USDC blacklist precedent: Circle has blacklisted addresses (Tornado Cash sanctions, Aug 2022). Aave market pauses: Aave has historically paused markets.
recommendation: (1) Split donation and addLiquidity into separate functions. (2) Wrap each external call in try/catch. (3) Document the operational playbook for emergency disablement.
severity_rationale: Carry-forward from report-6 (Medium). Function availability of the protocol's primary value-flow mechanism (LP add) halted by an unrelated impairment of the donation leg. Mainnet realism is strong. Medium per C4.
poc_notes: PoC from report-6 still applies. 5 tests pass: healthy sanity baseline; USDC blocklist DoS; Aave waUSDC pause DoS; donation pool depleted; recovery requires owner intervention.
